previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for post-procedural monitoring following bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the trachea and bilateral mainstem bronchi due to recurrent tracheal stenosis from Meyhre’s syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. He tolerated the procedure well and was observed for airway stability and pain management. Initial leukocytosis improved without signs of acute infection. Bronchial cultures grew Serratia marcescens and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, interpreted as colonization; thus, systemic antibiotics were avoided and inhaled tobramycin was continued. Chest imaging showed no complications. His pain resolved by hospital day 3, and he was discharged home on scheduled and as-needed pain control, with continuation of all home medications and follow-up arranged with pulmonology and rheumatology.

#Tracheobronchomalacia s/p balloon dilatation of trachea and LMS
#Acute hypercarbic respiratory failure (resolved)
___ syndrome
History of tracheobronchomalacia and stenosis requiring serial 
balloon dilations. He presented to the medicine floor following 
a planned bronchoscopy with dilation of the left mainstem to 9 
mm and trachea to 12 mm, as well as tracheostomy exchange with 
placement of a longer trach, the ___ 9 ID 12.3 OD to bypass 
initial stenosis. He was monitored overnight and treated with 
oxycodone and Tylenol for pain control. During hospital day 1, 
the patient developed desaturations to ~85% associated with 
profound AMS with minimal responsiveness. CXR normal, ABG showed 
significant hypercarbia (pH 7.07/CO2 119). The patient was 
placed on 100% FiO2, then bagged through his trach, and given 
narcan x1 with mild improvement in mental status. IP then took 
the patient for urgent repeat bronchoscopy that showed outward 
displacement of his tracheostomy with distal tracheal stenosis. 
The trach was replaced to 1cm above the carina and sutured into 
place. He was placed on the vent and monitored in the ICU. On 
___ he was bronched at the bedside in the ICU showing the trach 
was in place. He was weaned off the vent by ___. On ___ 
bedside exam revealed that the trach had become displaced 
outward by 1cm. Had repeat bronch ___ with tracheostomy 
exchange. IP could not pass distal stenosis with ___, instead 
 placed a shorter 9 portex. Underwent dilation of LMS bronchus 
and distal tracheal stenosis. He was monitored with respiratory 
stability for >24 hours. His respiratory status improved and he 
was weaned off the ventilator transferred to the floor for pain 
control on his home trach mask. He was continued on home 
duonebs, prednisone, and tobramycin nebs. He received oxycodone, 
acetaminophen, and ibuprofen for pain control and IV dilaudid 
was added for breakthrough. He tolerated these without 
somnolence.

#Atrial Flutter
During this admission, he had a ___ minute period of atrial 
flutter on telemetry which was asymptomatic. He has no known 
history of AFib. He had a TTE which showed LVEF >= 75% and 
increased PCWP, no clear cause of his atrial flutter. He had a 
TSH which was normal. He should have follow up with a cardiac 
monitor after discharge. He was not started on anticoagulation 
as CHADS-VASc score 0.
